claims.claim: pm_taxCO2eqSum(ttot,all_regi) is declared in 46_carbonpriceRegi, in both the none and netZero realizations; units T$/GtC, ×272 gives $/tCO2
The main calculation is core/presolve.gms:10 as pm_taxCO2eq + pm_taxCO2eqRegi + pm_taxCO2eqSCC, with a 2030 cap applied just below it
claims.note: The sum is correct. The 2030 cap sits inside $ifThen cm_CO2PriceLimit, and that switch defaults to off, so the cap does nothing in the default configuration. The answer doesn't say this.

claims.claim: The parameter is initialised to 0 in core/datainput.gms:13 and reset to 0 in core/preloop.gms:44
claims.note: The answer says 'each preloop iteration', but preloop runs once, before the iteration loop. The line reference itself is correct.

claims.claim: core/postsolve.gms:51-56 overwrites it from the dual value q_co2eq.m (a Nash-mode derivation), with a special case for years before 2025
claims.note: Both assignments are guarded by cm_emiscen. The dual-value derivation runs only when cm_emiscen eq 6 (it has both a negishi and a nash branch, so calling it 'Nash-mode' is wrong). The pre-2025 case runs only when cm_emiscen eq 1. The default is cm_emiscen = 9, so neither overwrite runs by default. The answer presents them as unconditional and later says the core computation 'lives in core/presolve.gms and core/postsolve.gms'.

claims.claim: 47_regipol/regiCarbonPrice conditionally zeroes or overrides it in presolve.gms:24 and postsolve.gms lines 151, 962, 976, 986, 1001
claims.note: regiCarbonPrice is the default realization. The writes are conditional (e.g. on cm_emiMktTarget), and the answer does say 'conditionally'.

claims.claim: The parameter is also 'touched' in 46_carbonpriceRegi/netZero/postsolve.gms:68, which back-calculates markup components (listed under where it is computed)
claims.note: Line 68 only reads pm_taxCO2eqSum, to compute p46_taxCO2eqRegiPeak. It does not write it. It belongs with the readers, and netZero is not the default realization (main.gms:418 sets none).

claims.claim: 21_tax (on) reads it in presolve, postsolve and equations to compute tax revenues for GHG, sector CO2, LUC, CDR and import markups
33_carbonRemoval (portfolio) reads it at equations.gms:316 to price net-negative CO2
47_regipol both reads it and writes it; it is aggregated into p47_taxCO2eq_AggEmi, p47_taxCO2eq_AggFE and p47_taxCO2eq_SectorAggFE
core reads it back at core/presolve.gms:256 to compute p_priceCO2
claims.note: The answer calls the result '$/tCO2', but the code multiplies by 1000, not 272. The 1000 factor gives $/tC. This unit detail is minor and isn't counted separately.

grade.went_well: The answer gets the declaring module right, names both realizations and gives correct line numbers. It locates the main computation at core/presolve.gms:10 with the correct formula. The reader list (core, 21_tax, 33_carbonRemoval, 47_regipol) is complete and every file:line citation is accurate. It keeps declared, populated and read separate, which is what the key asks for.
grade.answer_key_issues: The key lists only core/presolve.gms:10 as the place the value is computed. The code has other writes: core/postsolve.gms:51-56 (only when cm_emiscen is 6 or 1, and the default is 9) and the 47_regipol/regiCarbonPrice overrides (presolve.gms:24; postsolve.gms:151, 962, 976, 986, 1001). The key's reader list also leaves out 46_carbonpriceRegi/netZero/postsolve.gms:68, which reads the parameter in a non-default realization.
grade.summary: The answer gets the declaration, the main computation (core/presolve.gms:10) and all consumer modules right, with accurate citations. Its main flaw is presenting the core/postsolve.gms overwrite from q_co2eq.m as an active computation site. That overwrite is guarded by cm_emiscen eq 6 (the pre-2025 case by eq 1), the default is cm_emiscen = 9, and it is mislabelled as 'Nash-mode'. Two smaller slips: it doesn't mention that the 2030 cap depends on cm_CO2PriceLimit (off by default), and it lists a read in 46/netZero as a write.
